Young Professionals pact: 300 professionals a year from each country, expandable to 500.

u0320.hook: EFTA's four = 'I Like Nice Sweets': Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland.

u0329.gist: President Droupadi Murmu made State Visits to Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania (July 19–25, 2026), the first Indian presidential visits to the first two.
facts: Dates: July 19–25, 2026; first Indian President to visit Moldova and North Macedonia.

u0330.gist: The India–UK CETA trade deal and Double Contribution Convention became operational on July 15, 2026, boosting trade, mobility and social-security relief.

UK service commitments: 12 sectors and 137 sub-sectors.
India kept dairy, cereals, millets, apples, edible oils and oilseeds out of major concessions.

mcq.q: The India–UK Double Contribution Convention (DCC), operational from July 15, 2026, mainly deals with:
o: Avoiding double taxation of company profits
Avoiding dual social-security contributions of posted workers
mcq.why: DCC prevents dual social-security contributions for eligible temporarily posted or detached workers.

mcq.q: How many chapters does the India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), operational from July 2026, have?
mcq.why: CETA is a next-generation free trade agreement with 30 chapters.

u0331.gist: PM Modi's Oslo visit (18–19 May 2026) raised India–Norway ties to a Green Strategic Partnership; Oslo also hosted the 3rd India–Nordic Summit.

u0340.gist: WJP Rule of Law Index 2026 (October 21, 2026) ranked India 88th of 143, down two places; Denmark topped.
facts: Released by World Justice Project on October 21, 2026; India 88th of 143, score 0.48.

India: 3rd of six in South Asia; best in Open Government (45th), worst in Civil Justice (116th).
Top: Denmark (0.90), Norway, Finland; last: Venezuela (143rd).

mcq.q: In the WJP Rule of Law Index 2026, released in October 2026, what was India's rank?
mcq.why: India ranked 88th among 143 countries with a score of 0.48, down from 86th.

u0341.gist: The 2026 Nobel Prizes were announced on October 5–12, 2026, in six fields; Peace went to Navi Pillay, a jurist of Indian Tamil origin.
facts: Medicine: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel — optogenetics (light-controlled neurons); announced 5 October.
Physics: Francis Halzen — IceCube Neutrino Observatory in Antarctic ice; high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.
Chemistry: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai — chirality (molecular handedness): asymmetric catalysis and autocatalysis.
Literature (8 October): Anne Carson, Canadian poet and classicist; works include Autobiography of Red, Nox.
Peace: Navi Pillay, South African jurist of Indian Tamil origin; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights 2008–2014.
Economics: Robert E. Hall (Stanford) and Michael Woodford (Columbia) — macroeconomic stabilisation (12 October).

mcq.q: Who received the Nobel Peace Prize 2026 for efforts to promote peace and international law?
mcq.why: Navi Pillay, South African jurist of Indian Tamil origin, won for promoting peace and international law.

mcq.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen for his role in which project?
mcq.why: Halzen played a decisive role in IceCube, which uses Antarctic ice to detect neutrinos.

u0342.gist: Global Hunger Index 2026 ranked India 100th of 122 countries (score 24.1, 'serious'); theme: 'No Security Without Food Security.'
facts: Released October 2026; 21st edition; first published in 2006.
Publishers: Concern Worldwide, Welthungerhilfe and IFHV.
India: 100th of 122, score 24.1 ('serious'); South Asia average 23.5, world 18.1.
Four indicators: undernourishment (1/3), child stunting (1/6), child wasting (1/6), under-five mortality (1/3).
India: child wasting 19.0% (main concern); stunting fell from 50% (2000) to 29.3%.
Last: Somalia (122nd, 47.0, 'alarming'); 24 countries share ranks 1–24.

u0342.trap: GHI score runs backwards: 0 is best, 100 is worst — a higher score means more hunger.

mcq.q: In the Global Hunger Index 2026, released in October 2026, what was India's rank?
mcq.why: India ranked 100th among 122 countries with a score of 24.1 ('serious').

u0343.gist: A WHO–UNICEF JMP report (September 22, 2026) on school water, sanitation and hygiene warns universal coverage by 2030 is unlikely.
facts: Released September 22, 2026: 'Progress on Drinking Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Schools 2015–2025'.
Tracks SDG Indicator 4.a.1; universal coverage means over 99%.
Global 2025: schools with basic water 78%, sanitation 77%, hygiene 72%.
India basic coverage: water 96.6%, sanitation 80.8% (2025); hygiene 52.9% (2024).
About 50 million Indian children lacked school sanitation — nearly one-fifth of the global 244 million.
India among 28 of 62 countries on track for universal basic drinking water.
u0343.trap: Needed speed-up: fourfold for water, fivefold for sanitation; for hygiene WHO says fourfold, parts of the JMP report say fivefold.

mcq.q: According to the WHO–UNICEF JMP report released in September 2026, what was India's basic drinking water coverage in schools (2025)?
mcq.why: India: drinking water 96.6% (2025), sanitation 80.8% (2025), hygiene 52.9% (2024).

u0344.gist: Scholars at Risk's Free to Think 2026 report (September 15, 2026) rated India's academic freedom 'severely restricted'; its AFI score fell to 0.14.

Five indicators include freedom to research and teach, institutional autonomy and campus integrity.
Same category as India: Hong Kong, Indonesia, Pakistan, West Bank, Ukraine.
u0344.trap: Free to Think is SAR's report; the Academic Freedom Index itself is run by FAU and the V-Dem Institute.

mcq.q: How did Scholars at Risk's Free to Think 2026 report classify academic freedom in India?
mcq.why: SAR classified India as 'severely restricted'; its AFI score fell from 0.16 to 0.14.

u0345.gist: WEF's 20th Global Gender Gap Report (September 16, 2026) ranked India 131st of 145 with 64.5% parity; Iceland topped again.
facts: India: 131st of 145, same rank as 2025; score up from 64.4% to 64.5%.

India's strongest: Educational Attainment 96.6%, Health and Survival 95.6%.

Iceland first (93.0%) for the 17th straight year; Chad last (145th).

u0345.hook: India's four pillars fall from school to parliament: Study 96.6, Health 95.6, Money 41.2, Power 24.5 (% parity).
u0345.trap: Rank 131st is unchanged from 2025; only the score moved (64.4% → 64.5%).

mcq.q: In WEF's Global Gender Gap Report 2026, released in September 2026, India ranked:
mcq.why: India ranked 131st among 145 economies with 64.5% parity, same rank as 2025.

u0346.gist: In September 2026 India endorsed the US-led 'Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security', joining the US and 24 other countries.

Other Indian top-10: Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Thrissur, Kochi, Kolkata, Kozhikode (499th).

mcq.q: In the Oxford Economics Global Cities Index 2026, which was India's highest-ranked city?
mcq.why: Delhi ranked 268th of 1,000 cities, ahead of Bengaluru (311th) and Mumbai (330th).

u0348.gist: On September 22, 2026, the US, Denmark and Greenland signed an Arctic Defense Agreement at the UN in New York, expanding US military access.
facts: Signed by Donald Trump, Danish PM Mette Frederiksen and Greenland PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
Amends the 1951 Defense Agreement (signed 27 April 1951) under the North Atlantic Treaty.
Earlier supplements: 1991 MoU and 2004 Igaliku Agreement.
Expands US activity at Pituffik Space Base (formerly Thule Air Base), north-western Greenland.
Recognises Denmark's sovereignty and Greenland's self-determination; refers to US Golden Dome missile defence.
Generally bars non-NATO countries from military bases in Greenland without the parties' agreement.
u0348.trap: Pituffik Space Base and Thule Air Base are the same place (old and new names).

mcq.q: The 2026 US–Denmark–Greenland Arctic Defense Agreement allows expansion of US military activity at which base, formerly called Thule Air Base?
mcq.why: It permits expansion at Pituffik Space Base, formerly Thule Air Base, in north-western Greenland.

u0349.gist: PM Modi attended the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek (August 31–September 1, 2026), which adopted the Bishkek Declaration in SCO's 25th anniversary year.
facts: Venue: Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic; chaired by President Sadyr Japarov; 28 documents approved.
India's approach: Security, Connectivity and Opportunity; backed English as an SCO official language.
India to host the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum later in 2026.
SCO set up June 15, 2001 (from Shanghai Five, 1996); 10 members; Secretariat in Beijing.
Joined: India and Pakistan 2017, Iran 2023, Belarus 2024; RATS is in Tashkent.
Pakistan holds 2026–27 presidency; Lahore named SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital 2026–27.
u0349.hook: India's SCO approach spells S-C-O: Security, Connectivity, Opportunity.
u0349.trap: Heads of State summit = 26th, Bishkek (Modi); Heads of Government meeting = 25th, Dushanbe (Rajnath Singh).

mcq.q: Which city was designated the SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026–27?
mcq.why: Pakistan took the 2026–27 presidency; Lahore was named SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital.

mcq.q: Where was the 26th SCO Council of Heads of State meeting held on August 31–September 1, 2026?
mcq.why: Modi attended the 26th SCO Heads of State meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic.

u0350.gist: India ranked 125th of 197 in Global Citizen Solutions' Global Passport Index 2026, slipping from 124th in 2025; Sweden topped.
facts: Index by Global Citizen Solutions, a private advisory firm; 14 indicators.
Weights: Enhanced Mobility 50%, Investment 25%, Quality of Living 25%.
India's score 45.1; Mobility 135th, Investment 94th, Quality of Living 118th.
Indian passport: free access 6, visa-on-arrival 10, e-visa 64, conventional visa 88 destinations.
Top: Sweden (96.05); last: Afghanistan (23.10).
India was 127th during 2021–2023.
u0350.hook: Weights 50–25–25: Mobility counts double, so it moves India's rank the most.

mcq.q: In Global Citizen Solutions' Global Passport Index 2026, what was India's rank among 197 countries and territories?
mcq.why: India ranked 125th, compared with 124th in 2025 and 127th during 2021–2023.

u0351.gist: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 131.1 points in July 2026, its highest since early 2023, driven by cereals, vegetable oils and sugar.
facts: FFPI: 131.1 points in July 2026, up 0.7 points (0.6%) from June.
Still 29.1 points (18.2%) below the March 2022 peak.
Tracks five groups: cereals, vegetable oils, meat, dairy, sugar; base period 2014–2016.
Cereals up 3.4% (wheat 5.8%); sugar up 5.6%; vegetable oils up 2.0%.
Meat fell 2.8% from its June record; dairy fell 0.7%.
Higher world food prices can push domestic inflation and complicate RBI policy.
u0351.trap: FFPI tracks international commodity prices, not domestic retail food prices.

mcq.q: Which organisation publishes the Food Price Index that averaged 131.1 points in July 2026?
mcq.why: The Food and Agriculture Organization reported the FFPI averaged 131.1 points in July 2026.

u0352.gist: UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2026 (July 7, 2026) said global FDI rose 6% to about US$1.6 trillion; India's inflows rose nearly 44%.
facts: Released July 7, 2026 by UNCTAD (UN Trade and Development); title 'International Investment in a Turbulent Era'.
Global FDI up 6% to about US$1.6 trillion in 2025, ending two years of decline.
India inward FDI: US$27.1 billion (2024) → US$38.9 billion (2025); rank 13th → 11th.
India outward FDI: US$24.3 billion → US$35.7 billion; rank 20th → 18th.
Top FDI destination 2025: United States ($277 billion), then Singapore.
FDI usually means at least 10% voting power (lasting interest).
u0352.trap: Inward FDI rank = 11th; outward FDI rank = 18th — don't swap.

mcq.q: According to UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2026, India's rank as an FDI destination in 2025 improved to:
mcq.why: India's inward FDI rose to US$38.9 billion in 2025, improving its rank from 13th to 11th.

u0353.gist: The US and Saudi Arabia signed a Section 123 civil nuclear agreement in July 2026, valid 30 years, without Saudi renouncing enrichment.
facts: Signed by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright (20 July, Washington) and Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman (22 July, Riyadh).
Legal basis: Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act, 1954.
Duration: 30 years after entry into force (Article 16).
Article 7: two-year joint study on enrichment; later enrichment needs written consent.
Unlike the 2009 US–UAE deal, Saudi Arabia has not renounced enrichment and reprocessing.
IAEA Additional Protocol not mandatory; Trump sent it to Congress on 24 August 2026.
u0353.trap: 'Gold Standard' = giving up enrichment and reprocessing. The 2009 US–UAE deal has it; the Saudi deal does not.

mcq.q: The US–Saudi Arabia civil nuclear agreement signed in July 2026 is based on Section 123 of which US law?
mcq.why: Its legal basis is Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act, 1954.

u0354.gist: On June 17, 2026, the US and Iran signed a 14-point MoU, an initial peace deal and ceasefire to end the four-month West Asia war.
facts: June 17, 2026: Trump and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian signed the 14-point MoU electronically; mainly a ceasefire.
Ends fighting on all fronts, including Lebanon; Strait of Hormuz reopens toll-free within 30 days.
Sanctions relief: US Treasury waivers let Iran export crude oil and petroleum products.
Nuclear: Iran halts enrichment and down-blends (dilutes) highly enriched uranium to 3.67% under IAEA monitoring.
Reconstruction fund of at least $300 billion, to be financed by Gulf Arab nations; US not directly.
US to unfreeze Iranian assets (Tehran seeks about $24 billion); 60-day talks for a final nuclear pact.
u0354.hook: Hormuz in 30 days, final nuclear deal in 60 days: the harder job gets double the time.
u0354.trap: $300 billion is the reconstruction fund (Gulf Arab money, not US); $24 billion is Iran's frozen assets.

mcq.q: Under the 14-point US–Iran MoU signed on June 17, 2026, to what level must Iran down-blend its existing highly enriched uranium?
mcq.why: Iran must halt enrichment and down-blend its highly enriched uranium to 3.67% under IAEA monitoring.

mcq.q: Under the US–Iran initial peace MoU of June 17, 2026, within how many days is passage through the Strait of Hormuz to be fully restored?
mcq.why: Free, toll-free passage through the Strait of Hormuz is restored to full capacity within 30 days.

u0355.gist: SIPRI Yearbook 2026 (57th edition, 8 June 2026) put India's nuclear stockpile at 190 warheads; India is the 5th largest military spender.
facts: Released 8 June 2026 by Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (founded 1966).
India: 190 warheads total stockpile, 12 deployed; Pakistan 170; China 620.
India's 2025 military spending: US$92.1 billion, up 8.9% — 5th largest.
Top spender: United States (954.0 billion, down 7.5%), then China, Russia, Germany.
Arms imports: Ukraine 9.7%, India 8.2% (2nd); exports: US 42.0%, France 9.8% (2nd).
World total inventory 12,187 warheads; Russia 5,420 and US 5,042 hold the most.
u0355.trap: India is the 2nd largest arms importer but the 5th largest military spender.

mcq.q: According to the SIPRI Yearbook 2026, what is India's share of global arms imports, making it the second-largest importer?
mcq.why: Ukraine led with 9.7%; India was second with 8.2% of global arms imports.

mcq.q: SIPRI estimated India's military expenditure in 2025 at:
mcq.why: SIPRI put India's 2025 military spending at US$92.1 billion, up 8.9% over 2024.

u0356.gist: IMD's World Competitiveness Ranking 2026 (June 18, 2026) placed India 44th of 70 economies, down from 41st; Singapore regained the top spot.
facts: Released June 18, 2026 by IMD Business School.
India fell three places: 41st (2025) → 44th (2026), out of 70.
Top five: Singapore, Hong Kong SAR, Switzerland, Taiwan, UAE.
Four pillars: Economic Performance, Government Efficiency, Business Efficiency, Infrastructure.
Vietnam joined in 2026 at 27th, taking the total to 70 economies.

mcq.q: In IMD's World Competitiveness Ranking 2026, India's rank was:
mcq.why: India fell three places from 41st in 2025 to 44th of 70 economies.

u0357.gist: QS World University Rankings 2027 (June 18, 2026): IIT Delhi (118th) stayed India's best; MIT first for the 15th year; India has 52 ranked institutions.
facts: Released June 18, 2026; more than 1,500 institutions in 106 countries and territories.
MIT top for the 15th consecutive year; Imperial College London and Stanford tied second.
India: 52 ranked institutions; fifth most represented after US, UK, mainland China, Germany.
IIT Delhi 118th (best Indian); IIT Bombay joint 134th; IIT Madras 170th.
IISc Bengaluru and IIT Kanpur both joint 221st.
Shoolini University joint 452nd: India's top private university, only one in global top 500.
u0357.trap: The edition is called '2027' but was released in June 2026.

mcq.q: Which Indian institution ranked highest in the QS World University Rankings 2027, released in June 2026?
mcq.why: IIT Delhi ranked 118th and remained the highest-ranked Indian institution.

u0358.gist: RSF's World Press Freedom Index 2026 ranked India 157th of 180, down six places from 151st, in the 'very serious' category.
facts: Released by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), covering 180 countries and territories.
India: 157th, score 31.96; was 151st in 2025.
India placed in the 'very serious' category.
Five indicators: political, legal, economic and sociocultural context, plus safety.
Top: Norway, Netherlands, Estonia; bottom: Eritrea (180th), North Korea (179th).
India below Nepal (87th), Maldives, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Pakistan (153rd).

mcq.q: In RSF's World Press Freedom Index 2026, India was ranked:
mcq.why: India ranked 157th of 180 (score 31.96), down six places from 151st in 2025.

u0359.gist: World Happiness Report 2026 (14th edition, March 19, 2026) ranked India 116th of 147; Finland was happiest for the ninth year in a row.
facts: Released March 19, 2026, ahead of the International Day of Happiness (20 March).
Published by Oxford's Wellbeing Research Centre with Gallup and UN SDSN.
Ranking based on the Cantril Ladder: people rate their life on a 0–10 scale.
Top five: Finland (7.764), Iceland, Denmark, Costa Rica, Sweden.
India 116th of 147; China 65th; last: Afghanistan (147th).
2026 focus: Social Media and Wellbeing.
u0359.trap: Happiness Day is 20 March; the 2026 report came out a day earlier, on 19 March.

mcq.q: In the World Happiness Report 2026, what was India's rank among 147 countries?
mcq.why: India ranked 116th out of 147 countries in the 2026 report.
